what: A full-panel 3D shape (the default is a hand built from primitive shapes) is rendered separately, and each 12px cell is stamped by brightness with one of five glyphs (cross, empty square, circle, pink cell, purple cell), rotating at .65 rad per second. Where the mouse passes, it spreads as fluid on a grid of 1/8 screen width (fading by .955 and .9 each step), and only that area is re-covered with glyphs while a white wireframe shows through. 450 pin-shaped dust particles flow in from z −12 to 12, and the whole scene gets a threshold 1 bloom (5 levels) and a 10-sample spectral chromatic aberration (1.1 + kick × 8 + (speed − 1) × .45). Holding down builds speed by .02~.6 per frame up to 20x (smoothDamp 1s · max 5/s), and releasing returns it to 1x. On enter (fx:enter), the camera approaches from 50 behind in 2s sine.out, and the dust and trails open in 3s power1.inOut.

options.start: load (default — opens as soon as attached) | enter (waits far off until fx:enter arrives at the document)
options.shape: hand (default) | knot | orb — 3D shape to dither
options.gain: Shape brightness multiplier (sum of the three spotlights), default 3.6 — raise it for more purple and pink cells
options.dust: Number of dust particles, default 450 — 0 means none
options.trail: If off, the mouse fluid trail is turned off
options.[data-fx-part=hint]: Optional text for the banner strip that rises at speed 7~10
options.fx:kick: When sent to the plate it kicks for .15s ÷ speed — 15% of the dust at 1.4x and 3x brightness, chromatic aberration +8, wire .02
options.fx:speed: On the board { value, lock } — Playback speed on release (.1x for the phone button and drawer). With lock, the press acceleration is locked.
options.fx:tick·fx:state·fx:ready: The panel launches it — tick { elapsed, scale, frames } Every frame, state { state: opening | experience }, ready fires after the first frame
options.--fx-glyph-1…5 · --fx-glyph-edge · --fx-: Five glyph colors, cell borders and wire color (by default derived from --kf-ink and --kf-accent)

use: Slows down when released ·
note: The original uses three/webgpu + TSL. Here, the WebGLRenderer of the same three build (0.180) and newly written GLSL produce the same values — the hand model, turbulence image and glyph image are built from basic shapes, value noise and canvas instead of the original files. On touch (hover false) the press acceleration is turned off (the button decides it via fx:speed), the camera shake is halved, and touch is not blocked. With reduced motion, only one fully opened scene is drawn. When loading three.cjs as a plain script, load three-global.js first — the class AudioContext inside it points to the browser’s own, so sound libraries like howler create their context before three.
